designs.title: UnitFold: per-call-site execution of GPU eBPF helpers, decided by load-time bytecode analysis

decisions.choice: SR: per-map linearizability over actions, where a recognised idiom unit is one atomic action and a deferred action linearizes at its GPU commit. The host-visible state is current at every host access through the map handler.
decisions.why: Linux allows exactly these histories plus lossy interleavings, so SR refines Linux. It makes today's 97-of-128 loss illegal and gives testable exact totals. It needs no kernel-completion hook, which graph launches would bypass.

decisions.choice: In the agent, in bpf_attach_ctx's CUDA link branch (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:636-648), between create_map_basic_info and create_attach_with_ebpf_callback, on raw eBPF bytecode, one link at a time.
decisions.why: This is the first point where the instructions, the map metadata and segment access are together. Rewritten instructions flow through the existing nv_attach_private_data.instructions with no interface change. Cross-program facts live in the handler in the segment, not in the last-link-wins map_basic_info.

decisions.choice: Port PR #624's forward worklist (registers, pointer provenance, map_fds, stack bytes) without PREVAIL. Replace its two-valued uniformity with a product lattice: constant/pointer kind, provenance scope with a timing flag, and value numbers.
decisions.why: It already tracks stack-resident keys per pc. The value numbers and constants are needed for idiom matching and format interning. PREVAIL is off in dev builds and gives no invariants back.

decisions.choice: A bytecode rewrite to registered helper ids 600-604. Site descriptors are immediates in argument registers (pc-free). Jump fixups are applied, and the rewrite is re-analysed with value-number comparison.
decisions.why: It avoids generate_ptx's missing hook, IR's missing pc, memcapture's pc shift and per-access recompiles, and the extern filter. O3 merging is harmless because descriptors are data. Unregistered ids are excluded by a containment test and a dlsym capability gate.

decisions.choice: Aggregation is done by exact run-time grouping on key bytes, using memory scratch, activemask, bar.warp.sync and popc. Static facts select only the popc fast path, and only for values that are invariant within a launch or a block.
decisions.why: Correctness then depends only on single-thread facts. The survey's own aggregatable column takes two inconsistent stances on %globaltimer. No ballot/shfl/match is needed, since their PTX acceptance after the retarget is untested.

decisions.choice: Fold on access: every bpf_map_handler entry point folds the key's pending GPU effects under the key's stripe lock before the host operation (Invariant I and the Fold lemma). get_next_key(NULL) folds everything.
decisions.why: Loader reads run in another process with no channel to the agent, and the request slot is unusable from the CPU. A fold done by the reader itself needs neither.

decisions.choice: Per-(map, agent) ledgers in the segment. Every word has one writer side: GPU atomics or stores, or CPU stores. Monotone D counters use CPU-side watermarks, and writer records use a seqlock. The 1527 fence discipline applies.
decisions.why: CPU-GPU atomicity on registered memory is open. The CUDA guide states that mapped-memory atomics are atomic only among GPU threads (external).

decisions.choice: res_lookup copies the slot's last written value plus the later adds into a stack scratch. It is valid only while the CPU-written per-map host epoch is unchanged since the write; otherwise LOOKUP_COPY, a host op that copies the value without returning a pointer.
decisions.why: Whether only GPU probes touch a map is unknowable at load time, so validity is checked dynamically. The stack copy keeps pointer reads after a delete working, as in cuda-counter's read of *tsp at pc 105.

decisions.choice: Any GPU site writing through a lookup pointer of M, atomic or not, keeps M out of DEFER. CPU programs may write through pointers only with atomic adds, and only next to add-only ledgers. Anything else flips M to SYNC.
decisions.why: Pointer stores bypass every hook (Invariant I), and a GPU atom.add through a pointer would meet the fold's CPU in-place add on the same word.

decisions.choice: A segment-wide generation counter in the handler, recorded in each ledger and in each fallback request. Close sets the ledgers DEAD and leaves them allocated.
decisions.why: fds are reused and modules never unload. Dropping effects of a closed map matches Linux, where the program still references the old, now unreachable map object.

decisions.choice: Unit-level fallback host ops (UNIT_ADD, UNIT_SET, UNIT_DEL, LOOKUP_COPY), one per group. The existing host_call protocol and its waiting rules are unchanged. Sync calls to ledgered maps add only an O(1) keyed fold and an epoch bump.
decisions.why: Fallbacks stay exact, so ledger-full and mode changes cost speed, not semantics. Runtime changes stay minimal.

decisions.choice: The ledger stays in pinned host memory. Costs (RTT, segment load and atomic latency under contention, device atomics, shape, PTX acceptance) are measured at start-up and feed the per-site cost model. A device-memory key-to-slot cache is optional. No kernel-completion-only device-home mode is offered.
decisions.why: Only host-visible ledgers let the loader fold without the agent. Hardware then enters only as cost parameters.

decisions.choice: Headline assertion: the per-record, oracle-free decision, cross-checked against the survey's operation and result_use. class is a stated function of decision and the external input cpu_reads_map. aggregatable is three-valued (yes/no/timing).
decisions.why: The class split is nearly vacuous given the input column. The simulation reproduces 20/39/0 and 0 decision and key_scope mismatches. The survey's 51 cannot be reproduced by any consistent rule: it is 47 yes plus 4 of the 8 timing sites.

decisions.choice: UPSERT_ADD and ADD_IF_PRESENT only: helper 600, add-only ledger, handler fold hooks, generation, pointer-writer flags, capability gate. Measured on CPU Hash lookup, CUDA Counter, threadscheduling and a new hash-counter micro case.
decisions.why: Smallest end-to-end piece with a visible exactness result (call_count 97 to 128) and speedups (about 339 to 50 us, about 2.88 to 1.76 ms, inferred), buildable in about five weeks.

risks: GPU atomics and stores on cuMemHostRegister'ed segment memory: the design assumes they are atomic among GPU threads (external, CUDA guide), visible to CPU acquire loads after membar.sys (inferred, same assumption as the request protocol and 1527), and seen whole as aligned 64-bit words (inferred; test T8). None of this has been measured on the Orin.

Cost of GPU atomics and loads on uncached segment memory under contention is unknown. A constant-key counter puts every warp on one word; the 300 us datum (CAS spinning by 32 warps) shows this can be bad. The ARRAY case (48 us) is only a proxy, so the speedups in R10 are inferences until the calibration runs.
O3 behaviour on LLVM 15's legacy pipeline: the claim that calls to different helper ids are never merged into one call is inferred, not checked. It must be confirmed by a PTX dump.

No slot reclamation in the first version: long-running applications with churning keys fill ledgers and fall back to sync. This stays exact but loses the speedup. Reclamation needs completion knowledge that graph launches hide.

Mode-flip window: a CPU plain store through a pointer that races a DEFER-to-SYNC flip can be ordered before GPU effects committed just before it. Closing it needs a CPU-GPU store-load handshake that is not established.

The survey's aggregatable column is internally inconsistent on %globaltimer (cuda-counter/rocm-counter yes, launchlate no). The 51 cannot be reproduced record by record by any consistent rule (47, 47 or 55).

The R7 result so far is a simulation with a hand-written provenance table, not the analyzer. The class check is nearly vacuous given cpu_reads_map as input; the decision cross-check is the real test, and it is only as good as the table.

Host-side changes alter segment-resident structures (handler gen and ledger pointer). The loader, the agent and every pass .so must come from the same build. A stale pass that reaches new helper ids would exit() the application; the dlsym gate mitigates this but is untested.

printk becomes asynchronous to the application's output (up to one watcher turn late, at most 1 ms with the park backstop). Tools that compare printk lines with application output in real time see a change from today's synchronous bpftime.
E2BIG corner: when a map is full, re-touched keys after a host delete are inserted in claim order, not arrival order. This is reported, not prevented.
Fold costs land on every host access to a ledgered map, and get_next_key(NULL) is O(capacity). Loader iteration latency grows with ledger size.
Multiple agents on one segment: only add kinds may span agents. The pre-existing shared CommSharedMem being zeroed by each agent is not fixed.
memcapture: res_lookup is disabled because memcapture's prepended stack stores are not mapped. Other attach types with unknown stack use need the same care.
The warp grouping scratch indexed by (%smid, %warpid) relies on a tag check against preemption (PTX may change %warpid, external). sm_61 (P40) correctness is argued, not tested.
Frozen maps: effects committed before a freeze are applied, as Linux would for program writes. Today's bpftime returns EPERM instead, so behaviour changes for that window.

The analyzer (~3k lines), the bytecode patcher with jump fixups, and the re-analysis by value numbers are the main implementation risk. Rule L must cover everything a unit defines, not only what the rewrite clobbers.

designs.title: Exact per-call-site execution of GPU eBPF helper calls: unit linearizability, commit-at-completion with merge-on-read, and a fence-only cut (semantics-first design)

decisions.choice: Unit linearizability. A unit is a recognized idiom, any other helper call, or one BPF_ATOMIC instruction; exact means a total order σ respecting program order and real time explains every returned value and the final state. Two stated carve-outs: C1 (in-flight reads of sharded ADD keys are regular and monotone) and C2 (closed maps).
decisions.why: Today's sync path loses counts, so it cannot be the reference. Every σ is a Linux-legal serial schedule, so this refines Linux while excluding lossy interleavings. It is testable with an oracle, and locality lets the proof be argued per key plus one host-owned presence/capacity object.

decisions.choice: Commit at unit completion into host-readable per-key slots in the shared segment. Every host access path in bpf_map_handler merges committed contributions on read.
decisions.why: Loader reads run in another process directly on the segment, with no channel to the agent. Merge-on-read needs no flush, no launch tracking and no live agent, so unnoted graph and CUDA 13 handle launches lose nothing. Completion events only drive printk drain, eager folding and the quiescent point.

decisions.topic: Ordering host writes against GPU effects
decisions.choice: A fence-only cut. The host writes the per-key control word (incarnation), fences, waits for the shard version to be even and seqlock-reads it. The GPU stores an odd version, does membar.sys, then reads the control word. Contributions carry incarnation tags.
decisions.why: No CPU-GPU atomic read-modify-write is needed (hostNativeAtomic is unknown, and occupy_flag is GPU-only). Store buffering gives exactly-one-side placement of every GPU unit relative to each host update, delete, lookup_and_delete, close or reclaim.

decisions.choice: Two-level: spin on a device-memory lock table allocated by the agent, then make uncontended stores of the host-visible version word.
decisions.why: Spinning on host memory cost 300 us against 10 us behind the device-memory module lock (CLAUDE.md:2185-2190). This copies host_call's own shape.

decisions.choice: ADD (add-or-create, add-if-present) uses per-(agent, SM) sharded slots and sums contributions. LWW (SET, DEL, READ) uses one unsharded slot with one owning agent. A map's kind is first-claim-wins in the segment, and conflicts go SYNC.
decisions.why: ADD is commutative, so sharding cuts contention. LWW needs one total order per key. Claims must live in the segment because modules cannot be unloaded and later programs, sessions and agents appear after hack_fatbin.

decisions.choice: A new synchronous ATTACH opcode executes the unit on the base map under the stripe lock (E2BIG check) and creates the slot. ABSENT slots act as a negative cache. Tombstones are folded before capacity-dependent host inserts.
decisions.why: It keeps presence and capacity a host-linearized object, covering the cross-key coupling through max_entries that per-key locality misses. It removes the first-touch race at the cost of one round trip per key, incarnation and warp group.

decisions.choice: Lanes active at the instruction with equal keys reduce their deltas; the leader commits the sum with count n. The key is proven uniform by the analyzer, or checked dynamically. Fallback is per-lane commits in the lane-turn loop, with no shfl.
decisions.why: It counts lanes rather than elections (upstream auto-warp counts one per converged group), so it is exact under divergence. It needs no match.any or redux, which are unverified in the retargeted module.

decisions.choice: In the agent: per-link facts in create_attach_with_ebpf_callback, then per-module consolidation and rewriting in hack_fatbin before the RuntimeRequest is built.
decisions.why: This is the first place with instructions, fd-indexed map_basic_info and the attach point together; all hook entries exist at hack_fatbin. It is the same location upstream PR #624 uses.

decisions.choice: Bytecode rewrite to new registered helper ids 520-525 with the site id as an immediate. In place when the region has room (NOP padding, no jump fixups); call-id swap for single calls; instruction insertion with branch-offset fixups otherwise. Rewritten words are self-validated, and the originals are used on any failure.
decisions.why: generate_ptx has no hook and IR has no eBPF pc. O3 and clang merge calls, memcapture shifts pcs, and unregistered ids exit the application through ExitOnError. Immediates survive all of these, and the patch-cache key changes automatically.

decisions.choice: READ_LOCAL copies the value into a stack slot of the probe's own frame, reserved by the analyzer, and returns its address.
decisions.why: Helpers are noinline and their locals die at return. cuda-counter's retprobe dereferences the pointer again at pc 105, after a delete, so the snapshot must live until program exit; this also avoids reading reused elements.

decisions.choice: Records in the survey schema plus decision, one per source-level call site (merged calls split per incoming flags edge). class is derived after joining the survey's cpu_reads_map; decision never depends on it. aggregatable: key scope ⊑ WARP for map ops, argument scope for printk.
decisions.why: Pre-check on records.json reproduces eliminate 20, defer 39, sync 0 and 36 of 38 map sites aggregatable. The survey's printk aggregatable is inconsistent on %globaltimer, so 51 is asserted as 47 plus 4 listed records.

decisions.choice: Define the protocol over lock, published and control memory with required properties A1-A5. Each placement gets capability bits from start-up litmus tests (MP both ways, SB, single-copy atomicity) and cost parameters (c_rt, c_pld, c_pst, c_fence, c_hld). The cost model picks the shard count, placement and folding.
decisions.why: Integrated and discrete GPUs differ only in placement and costs. On discrete GPUs the placement changes how the cut executes, not the proof, provided the capability bits hold.

decisions.choice: ADD only (shapes A, B, C and H-lookup) on HASH, gated by step-0 litmus tests. Measured on micro CPU Hash map lookup, a new CPU Hash counter case, CUDA Counter and threadscheduling. Tests T1-T8 use σ oracles, plus mutations M1-M12.
decisions.why: It is the smallest piece that exercises every load-bearing mechanism (merge, cut, ATTACH, aggregation, rewrite) against a known oracle. Expected per-launch times are anchored to the measured array direct path (47-48 us against 317-341 us for today's hash cases).

risks: The store-buffering guarantee between CPU and GPU on cuMemHostRegister'ed memory (A3: GPU st; membar.sys; ld against CPU st; dmb; ld) is unproven. The whole cut rests on it; if the step-0 litmus fails, PES is disabled and every site stays synchronous.

GPU load, store and fence costs to registered host memory are unknown; the only datum is the 300 us against 10 us contention figure. If they are large, a per-warp commit approaches a host call and the R10 expectations (50-60 us per launch) move.

C1 (corrected): in-flight host reads of sharded ADD keys are regular and monotone, not linearizable, even for unit-increment counters, because a group commit adds n at once. They are linearizable only with a stable double collect (unchanged ver), S = 1, or at quiescence.
shfl.sync and vote.sync.ballot after the sm_61 to sm_87 retarget are unverified. The lane-turn per-lane fallback keeps exactness but costs more.

Bytecode idiom recognition is shape-specific: other clang versions may emit shapes outside the patterns, and those sites stay SYNC (sound but slow). Translation validation (T8) only guards the unsound direction.

Merged call instructions (cuda-counter retprobe pc 76 serves source lines 76 and 79) require per-edge records. Line mapping needs .BTF.ext, which the syscall server does not store, so only the offline check has line numbers; rocm-counter must be built for the check.

The survey's printk aggregatable field is internally inconsistent on %globaltimer (cuda-counter/rocm-counter against launchlate), so 51 can only be reproduced as an analyzer count plus four listed records.

The bounded wait on an odd shard version holds a host stripe lock. A long GPU preemption delays every host operation on that stripe; liveness-based recovery (committed half selected by ver) covers only dead owners.
Several agents on one segment still share one CommSharedMem request slot, zeroed by each agent (pre-existing). ATTACH and the remaining sync calls inherit that hazard until a per-agent slot exists.

The PES ABI changes the segment layout (directory, map_uid in the handler) and adds helper ids and an opcode. Mixed runtime versions on one segment must be refused, and old watchers cannot serve ATTACH.
The device-memory lock table is reachable only from kernels in the agent's context [inferred]. Modules loaded into other contexts need their own table or stay SYNC.

On CUDA-IPC (discrete) platforms, 1501's staging-copy lookup and its never-succeeding NOEXIST insert must be fixed (a keyed add-or-create and insert for nv_gpu_shared_hash_map_impl) before deferral can target it.

designs.title: Fused call sites and merge-on-read overlays: per-call-site execution of GPU eBPF helpers (performance and code generation first)

decisions.choice: SIS: per-operation sequential consistency whose unit is the recognized idiom (A/B/C -> add_or_create, H -> add_if_exists). Host reads are linearized when they read the overlay; observation points are every loader map command, every CPU-probe helper call, every watcher request, kernel completion, and the printk drain bound.
decisions.why: Today's bpftime loses counts (calls=97 = 4x32-31), and Linux's S1 permits that, so it cannot measure exactness. Full serializability of whole probe executions would be broken by the sync path itself. Idiom-level units make 128 the only exact answer and keep Linux's semantics everywhere else.

decisions.choice: Single-writer rule: every overlay word is written either only by GPU threads (GPU atomics) or only by CPU parties (under the base map's stripe lock). CPU writes record offsets and versions instead of resetting GPU words.
decisions.why: CPU-GPU atomicity on registered memory is unknown (hostNativeAtomicSupported not queried), the CPU cannot RMW device memory on PCIe, and the loader must not post into CommSharedMem. This follows the 1527 ringbuf's head/tail split.

decisions.topic: Dynamic answer to 'only GPU probes touch this map'
decisions.choice: A per-map overlay of pending GPU effects. Every CPU reader merges it on access (loader syscall server, CPU probes, watcher). A cpu_write_seq word guards GPU-confined reads. Map states PLAIN / OVERLAY / SEALING->PLAIN.
decisions.why: The merge lives in libbpftime's map layer, so the loader process runs it directly on the segment without a channel to the agent. The loader's access pattern is never needed at load time.

decisions.choice: Rewrite the agent's copy of the bytecode into private fused helper ids with the site id as an immediate in a free argument, padded with ja +0. Non-contiguous regions get the call in the head chunk and a ja to the join. Gated on the pass reporting the ids.
decisions.why: The decision survives O3 call merging (a non-constant site id falls back to the generic fused helper), memcapture's pc shift and the absence of pcs in IR. It also changes the patch-cache key, and an unregistered id cannot exit() the application.

decisions.choice: Tier 0: generic fused helpers in the trampoline, with warp primitives as inline-asm PTX text. Tier 1: an IR inlining pass hooked between optimizeModule and codegen in generate_ptx via the llvmbpf patch overlay, which constant-folds the delta, the key kind and pre-resolved slots.
decisions.why: Tier 0 is correct alone and needs no llvmbpf change. Tier 1 removes the call overhead and the hash probe for module-constant keys. Inline asm avoids LLVM 15's sm_61 NVPTX selection limits.

decisions.choice: Group lanes at run time with match.any.sync. Count = popc(group); 64-bit sum = three redux.sync.add.u32 over 22/21/21-bit limbs (or popc x c for a constant delta); one posted red.add of sum and count per group, with no per-op fence. Per-lane red.add fallback.
decisions.why: Soundness must not depend on static uniformity (globaltimer, smid). redux is 32-bit only, and the limb split keeps 64-bit sums exact. red is posted, which matters on uncached sysmem.

decisions.choice: Construction classes (grid / block / warp / lane; 509 block-uniform, 510 warp-uniform, 502 lane-varying, map-value loads take the key's class only for maps no GPU site writes) are used for reporting and for skipping match.any on module-constant keys.
decisions.why: These classes reproduce the survey's key_scope for all 38 map operations. Grouping correctness never depends on them.

decisions.choice: Overlays get next_pow2(2 x max_entries) slots, capped per map and by a segment budget. printk rings are per agent and per SM. A per-module __bpftime_site[1024] table is written on all three module-global paths. When full: exact synchronous fallback for map units; backpressure (drain-then-print) for printk.
decisions.why: Sizing never depends on the grid, so unnoted graph launches and CUDA 13 handle launches cannot overflow a launch-time size. Map units are never dropped silently.

decisions.choice: A key is admitted at its GPU slot claim with a conservative bound (gpu_claims + base_keys_at_creation + cpu_new_keys <= max_entries). Over the bound, the unit goes to a synchronous request where the host applies E2BIG on the merged state.
decisions.why: Membership is stable and identical for GPU and CPU readers, and never exceeds max_entries. The conservatism costs speed only.

decisions.choice: Kept. New host request types execute idiom units on merged state (drain-first by construction). Synchronous printk drains rings first. Optional warp-batched requests: one round trip per group, executed in lane order.
decisions.why: This is the soundness fallback. Batching cuts 32 round trips to 1 without changing per-lane results.

decisions.choice: In the agent: per program in create_attach_with_ebpf_callback, per map in init_attach_ctx_from_handlers (eligibility over all cuda__ handlers), per module at hack_fatbin (site ids, site table). Plus an offline CLI with BTF line info for the survey check.
decisions.why: The agent is the first place with instructions, map descriptors and the attach type together, and it sees every program handler. PREVAIL is too slow and rejects fetch atomics.

decisions.choice: cpu_reads_map is an explicit input (runtime bit online). Records are deduplicated on (file, line, section, helper), with one record per incoming arm for shared calls. Expected: class 109/20/39/0 exact; aggregatable 47 (sound) or 53 (upstream timer rule), not 51.
decisions.why: B total_time and B call_count differ only in whether the loader reads the map. The survey's aggregatable column treats %globaltimer and a GPU-written *tsp inconsistently across sites.

decisions.choice: A start-up calibration kernel, cached per device in the segment (c_rt, same- and distinct-address red throughput, c_ld, c_dtoh, feature flags), picks grouping, SM-sharding, inline vs call, placement and sync batching. Sync on cost only for a discrete-GPU map also touched by CPU probes when sysmem reductions over PCIe are not exact.
decisions.why: On the Orin an admissible fused site beats a ~10 us round trip by orders of magnitude, so the model optimizes the form of the fast path rather than trading exactness.

decisions.choice: Agent-owned device-memory overlays with an IPC handle for loader reads (cuMemcpyDtoH), a 100 ms segment mirror plus mirrors at detach and exit, and printk rings in pinned host memory.
decisions.why: Server-owned device memory would fault the application's kernels if the loader exits first. Agent ownership bounds crash loss to the mirror period.

decisions.choice: Step 0 (PTX acceptance, host-call breakdown, red throughput, CPU visibility, two-process atomicity), then idiom A only, Orin, tier 0, with merged HASH operations in libbpftime. Programs: cuda-counter, threadscheduling and a new hash-counter micro mode, with a witness-ring oracle and 8 mutations.
decisions.why: It exercises every layer (analyzer, rewrite, trampoline, overlay, merge in the loader) on the smallest idiom, with a crisp exactness check (calls 97 -> 128) and large measurable speedups on the micro mode.

risks: PTX text for match.any.sync, redux.sync, red.global.add and nanosleep may be refused in the retargeted module (.version 8.1, .target rewritten to sm_87); this is untested. The fallback is per-lane red.add, which is still exact but has no aggregation.

Atomicity of GPU reductions on cuMemHostRegister'ed memory across two CUDA contexts (two agents), and the visibility of posted reductions to CPU readers on the Orin, are unmeasured. The design assumes only GPU-GPU atomicity and single-copy-atomic aligned 64-bit reads.

All speedups are estimates from analogs (CPU Array 320-371 -> 49-51 us; 1513 lookup/update at 100k and 1M threads). The uncached reduction throughput and the internal breakdown of the ~10 us host call have never been measured on the Orin.

Baseline numbers are from aa6eb973 (sets N of baseline-sub and hostcall-l1). 52126f33 adds the AC3 watcher (11.8 us per call in bursts without load, 15.7 under load), so slice-1 comparisons must re-measure D at 52126f33.

The survey's aggregatable count of 51 cannot be reproduced by any consistent uniformity rule: 47 if %globaltimer is lane-varying, 53 with upstream's table. The survey needs a correction, not the analyzer.
Every CPU map helper and loader map command gains an overlay check, and maps with overlays gain merge work on every CPU access. CPU-probe hot paths could regress; this is unmeasured.
SEALING (a late GPU program with an unfusible site on an overlaid map) needs quiescence. With unseen launches (graphs, CUDA 13 handles) the late link is deferred, perhaps indefinitely.
The admission bound is conservative after deletes, so churn-heavy maps fall back to the synchronous path more often until a quiescent reclaim, which also needs every writer agent to be quiescent.

Changing the segment ABI (overlay objects, header words, format table) means mixed runtime versions on one segment are unsupported. Regenerating trampoline_ptx.h and two trampoline variants (sm_70+ and below) add build surface.

Bytecode rewriting depends on exact pattern conditions (no jumps into regions, room in the head chunk, an R0 def-use that is complete through spills). An analyzer bug could miscompile silently, so the witness-ring oracle and the mutations are essential.
GPU_READ is disabled for memcapture programs (r10 is shifted by captured-line lengths the agent does not know). memcapture's many sites also stress the code-size budget.

On discrete GPUs an agent killed by SIGKILL loses up to 100 ms of overlay deltas. Loader-side IPC import needs a CUDA context in the loader process, and whether an 8-byte DtoH read is single-copy atomic against concurrent reductions is unverified.
printk deferral changes real-time interleaving with host output, which matters for tools like launchlate that compare CPU and GPU prints. BPFTIME_GPU_PRINTK_SYNC=1 keeps today's behaviour.
Fixed per-module site table (1,024 entries, 32 KiB device global) and the module's constant bank are shared with application globals. Sites beyond the table are not fused.

strengths: Its core needs only memory facts the code already relies on at 52126f33. Host ops fold each pending effect under the key's stripe lock. Adds sit in single-writer, monotone u64 words (one D per map and agent), and the CPU keeps its own watermarks. This uses GPU atomics on segment memory (occupy_flag atomicCAS, default_trampoline.cu:149) and fence-then-flag message passing in both directions (default_trampoline.cu:152-166). A host write needs only single-word coherence: an add the fold does not see is ordered after the write. No CPU-GPU store buffering and no mixed CPU-GPU atomics are needed.
Ledgers are per (map, agent), so only one GPU context ever writes a given D. That avoids the cross-context atomicity question that performance-first leaves open.
Of the three, its decisions are the most per-site. SET, DEL and res_lookup can mix with adds on one key inside one agent's ledger, ordered by wD; only the add kind is fixed per map.

It is the only design that confronts plain pointer stores, which bypass every hook. The analyzer classifies them into gpu_ptr_writer and cpu_ptr_writer, and only CPU atomic adds are allowed next to add-only ledgers.

Its GPU-local reads are sound. res_lookup is validated by a host-mutation epoch. The LOOKUP_COPY fallback returns no pointer, so reads do not bump the epoch and thrash. res_lookup is disabled under memcapture.

Its code citations check out. The analyzer placement (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:636-648, between create_map_basic_info and create_attach_with_ebpf_callback) is right. The dlsym capability gate sits next to print_config and process_input (nv_attach_impl.cpp:601-614). The four-digit extern filter is at core.cpp:280-283, and the static ExitOnError at llvm_jit_context.cpp:907,936-939.

Its R7 is honest. The decision field needs no oracle, and the design states that class is nearly vacuous given cpu_reads_map. aggregatable is three-valued (47 yes, 8 timing, 4 no). The simulation (r7_output.txt) reproduces 20/39/0 with 0 decision mismatches.
Close and fd reuse are handled by a gen counter and a DEAD mode. map_info holds only a pointer to live state, so module snapshots never go stale. Graph launches do not matter for correctness.
It explains today's loss correctly: 97 = 4 x 32 - 31 first-touch losses, matching calls=97 (hostcall-l1-20261111/README.md:30-31; compare-20261110/README.md:87).
flaws: The fold-hook list omits the typed HASH fast paths. CPU programs whose map calls all target HASH get the typed helpers (selected at bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:499-555). Those call map_lookup_hash, map_update_hash and map_delete_hash (map_handler.cpp:302,336,355, via bpf_helper.cpp:492,595,621), bypassing map_lookup_elem (:135), map_update_elem (:441) and map_delete_elem (:773). So "every path converges there" is false as cited. A CPU-probe update(ANY, X) skips the fold, and a later fold adds effects committed before the update on top of X, violating SR [inferred, not run]. This is a fixable omission.

Upsert presence is derived from ΔD alone; the slot has no count. A group with Σd = 0 (zero delta, or deltas that cancel or wrap mod 2^64) on an absent key leaves D unchanged. After a host delete, the fold then cannot recreate the key, although Linux's NOEXIST insert would. Shape B's delta is a %globaltimer difference (cuda-counter retprobe pc 17-21). [inferred, not run]

The DEFER-to-SYNC flip has a check-then-commit race. A helper checks mode == DEFER and then commits. When a late GPU pointer-writer link flips the map, effects that passed the check land after the flip-time fold. Later folds apply them with a CPU in-place add on the element, while the new program does atom.add through device aliases (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:136-144). That mixes CPU and GPU atomics on one word, which BRIEF lists as open. The design closes only the CPU plain-store window (its deviation 3).

With several agents, the fold reads each agent's D at a different instant. A host read can include agent 2's add but miss agent 1's add that preceded it in real time, which breaks its own SR rule 3 (real-time order). The design does not acknowledge this; semantics-first admits the same anomaly as C1.

The SET/DEL fold is never specified ("R6 gives the fold function" is not true of R6). An in-place write tears for lock-free lookups (bpftime_hash_map.hpp:112-134). A replace (:528-538) is Linux-like but must be stated. The loader's lookup copies the value with memcpy after the lookup returns, outside any lock (syscall_context.cpp:615-622). That copy can race an in-place ADD fold run by another process.

Each key has one D word per agent on uncached segment memory, so every warp on a hot constant key hits one word. The trampoline's own comment reports 300 us instead of 10 under that kind of contention (default_trampoline.cu:118-122). There is no sharding option, and the R10 numbers depend on an unmeasured c_atom_sys.
The printk ring lives in agent-private pinned memory, not the segment. Lines from kernels still running more than 100 ms after agent exit are lost, and there is no orphan drain.

strengths: It has the most precise reference semantics. Unit linearizability gets explicit program-order, real-time and sequential-spec clauses. Two carve-outs are stated: C1 (in-flight reads of sharded ADD keys are regular and monotone) and C2 (closed maps). The proof sketch uses lemmas L1-L4 plus Herlihy-Wing locality. It alone treats presence and capacity as a host-linearized object (L4), so the cross-key coupling through max_entries is covered.

The hardware assumptions A1-A5 are tabulated with today's evidence for each. They are gated by start-up litmus tests run against a CPU thread in another process, and every site stays synchronous if they fail. This is the most reviewer-proof stance.

Its host hook list is complete. It includes the typed fast paths map_lookup_hash, map_update_hash and map_delete_hash (map_handler.cpp:302-367, called from bpf_helper.cpp:470-622), verified against the code.
Each commit carries the count n together with the sum, under a device-memory lock and a seqlock. Creation is therefore correct for any delta, including zero.

Per-agent shards, a single owning agent per LWW map, map_uid in the site table, close cutting every slot to CLOSED, liveness-based recovery of dead owners, and an orphan printk drain by the loader together cover R9 most completely.
Its R2 is the strongest. It lists contributions and argues that aggregation counts lanes, not elections (L3).
Its test plan is the strongest. Tests use σ oracles, T2 checks real-time completeness, T8 does translation validation against the CPU JIT, and 12 mutations include one on the check script itself.

Its code reading is accurate. Frozen-map EPERM is at map_handler.cpp:445-448 and 776-779; helper registration at core.cpp:234-253; the extern filter at :280-283. The memcpy-free merging copy for loader lookups (syscall_context.cpp:615-622) is called out.
flaws: The whole cut (L1) rests on CPU-GPU store buffering (A3). There is no evidence for it at 52126f33: today's request protocol uses only fence-then-flag message passing (default_trampoline.cu:152-166). If the step-0 litmus fails, nothing is deferred. The core mechanism therefore relies on an open item, which is the decisive difference from analysis-first.

As written, L1 loses data [inferred, not run]. The host loads an even ver and reads the committed half, which holds the old incarnation's sum. Suppose one GPU commit that already saw inc+1 lands before the host re-reads ver. It finds h.tag != c.inc, resets h to {inc+1, 0, 0}, writes the other half and bumps ver. The host retries, reads the new committed half (tag inc+1) and counts 0. The old incarnation's contributions are then counted on neither side. Hot keys make this likely.

READ_LOCAL reserves a stack slot "below the deepest used offset" and self-validates it as "inside 512 B" on the rewritten words. That check runs before memcapture prepends its instructions, which store at r10-8, do `r10 -= len` with SUB64_IMM and store the captured PTX line (ptxpass_kprobe_memcapture/main.cpp:63-127). Under memcapture the reserved slot can therefore fall outside the frame. The other two designs disable their stack-copy read there.

Under C1, the counters the host reads most (call_count) get only regular reads when sharded. Linearizable reads need S = 1, which brings back the single-word contention that sharding was meant to remove.

The cut waits on an open GPU section while holding the HASH stripe spinlock, which CPU probes in the application and the loader also take. The wait is bounded only by the owner's liveness: a preempted warp or a debugger stalls host paths.

A CPU plain store through a folded pointer goes to base, and GPU contributions that completed before the store are later merged on top of it (base ⊕ shards). No hardware interleaving under Linux gives that outcome. The design only says plain stores are "left to the hardware memory model".

It has the most mechanisms: directory, key index, incarnations, two halves, watermarks per agent and shard, hseq, a new ATTACH opcode, bounded waits and orphan recovery. Its first slice saves only about 32 x 11 us per CUDA Counter launch.
The litmus exit rule ("the negative control must show violations, or the test is too weak") could block a correct design on hardware that happens to be stronger than required.
One citation is off: "every 1000 us, or 100 us with WFE: cuda_watcher_policy.hpp:27-28". Line 26 is slow_sleep_us = 100, line 27 park_backstop_us = 1000 and line 28 event_query_every_us = 1000.

strengths: It has the best performance engineering. Lanes are grouped with match.any.sync. A constant delta becomes popc x c, and 64-bit sums are exact via three redux.sync.add.u32 over 22/21/21-bit limbs. Each group issues one posted red, with a per-lane fallback.

It adds a tier-1 IR inlining step through the existing llvmbpf overlay, mirroring the CPU JIT's array inlining. It also proposes warp-batched synchronous requests: one round trip per warp group for the sites that stay synchronous.

Its projections are anchored to measured analogs and carry the right baseline caveat (aa6eb973 against 52126f33 with the AC3 watcher). The numbers check out: 327.5 / 341.1 / 317.7 us (hostcall-l1-20261111/README.md:38), CUDA Counter 2,928.9 us (baseline-sub-20261111/summary.md:22) and calls=97.
Eligibility is computed over all cuda__ handlers at init_attach_ctx_from_handlers. Storage is never sized by the grid.
Its test ideas are strong: a witness-ring oracle, a step-0 breakdown of host_call by %globaltimer stamps, and large-geometry cases.
It correctly disables GPU_READ under memcapture because of the r10 SUB64_IMM shift. Its single-writer word rule follows the 1527 head/tail split.
flaws: SIS has no real-time clause, only program order plus "globally performed". O1 ("includes every GPU effect globally performed before the read") is circular. With fence-free posted reductions, the only guarantee during a kernel is close to gpu_ext's completion-time visibility, which weakens the R2 claim of "exact, not eventual".

Even plain sequential consistency fails [inferred]. One thread's posted red.add to map M and LWW store to map N have no fence between them, so the loader can see N's store and miss M's add. The claimed total order consistent with program order then does not exist.

sum and count are two unordered posted reductions [inferred, not run]. A CPU delete can snapshot off_sum after a group's sum has landed but off_count before its count lands. Afterwards count - off_count > 0, and the key reappears as corr + 0, a state no serial order produces. Reads can likewise see count without sum. This is an exactness bug in the headline counter idiom.

The E2BIG admission check is a store-buffering pattern with no stated fence. The GPU reads cpu_new_keys and then bumps gpu_claims, while the CPU does the mirror image. Both can admit, and the merged membership exceeds max_entries [inferred]. This relies on an open item.

Eligibility is per map, not per site: one unfusible GPU site anywhere makes the whole map PLAIN. A late unfusible link on an OVERLAY map needs SEALING and quiescence. With unseen launches (graphs; CUDA 13 handles, nv_attach_impl.cpp:1561-1592) the late link is deferred, possibly forever. That is an R9 behaviour change the other two designs do not have.

The merge layer is named only as "libbpftime's map layer", with no entry points. The typed fast paths (map_handler.cpp:302-367, selected at bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:499-555) bypass the generic dispatchers, and the design never says how they are covered.

On the Orin, overlays are shared per map across agents, which relies on GPU atomics on segment memory being atomic across CUDA contexts [inferred]. Its fast path also relies on no-fence posted-red visibility to CPU readers and on PTX-text acceptance of match.any and redux, all open in BRIEF. On discrete GPUs, device-memory overlays lose up to 100 ms of deltas on an agent SIGKILL, which is not exact.
A CPU plain store through a materialized pointer has the same overlay-on-top outcome as in semantics-first.
Its headline CUDA Counter number (60-90 us) needs four slices. Slice 1 removes one of eight host calls per thread.

grafts: From semantics-first, take the reference-semantics machinery and wrap it around UnitFold's fold mechanism: unit linearizability (program order, real time, sequential spec), the explicit carve-outs (C1 for multi-ledger or sharded reads, C2 for close), the lemma-plus-locality proof, and presence and capacity as a host-linearized object (L4).

From semantics-first, take the hardware-assumption table with today's evidence for each row, gated by start-up litmus tests against a CPU thread in another process (message passing in both directions, single-copy 64-bit atomicity, plus store buffering if any part still needs it). Deferral is switched off per capability bit.

From semantics-first, take the host hook list (R3.4): the HASH branches of map_lookup_elem, map_update_elem and map_delete_elem, the typed map_lookup_hash, map_update_hash and map_delete_hash (map_handler.cpp:302-367), lookup_and_delete (:1797), get_next_key (:617) and the diagnostic paths. The loader's lookup should become a merging copy instead of pointer plus memcpy (syscall_context.cpp:615-622).
From semantics-first, take the count carried with the sum, so that upsert creation does not depend on Σd ≠ 0. Also take the ABSENT negative cache for add-if-present and delete of absent keys.
From semantics-first, take map_uid in the site table, the per-agent liveness record with orphan recovery, and the orphan printk drain by the loader or the next agent.

From semantics-first, take the tests: σ-oracle tests, T2 real-time completeness with CLOCK_MONOTONIC stamps, T8 translation validation (the original program run in the llvmbpf CPU JIT over random serial schedules), and a mutation of the survey-check script itself.
From semantics-first, take the recommendation to replace the static ExitOnError in generate_ptx (llvm_jit_context.cpp:907,936-939) with error propagation.
From semantics-first, take the ATOMIC_LOCAL extension: plain RMWs on GPU-local maps that lose counts today (mem_trace, ARRAY (*v)++) become atomics.

From performance-first, take the fast path: match.any.sync grouping, popc x c for constant deltas, exact 64-bit sums by redux on 22/21/21-bit limbs, and a per-lane fallback, enabled by step-0 PTX acceptance tests.
From performance-first, take warp-batched synchronous requests for the sites that stay synchronous. Lane order is kept and the warp pays one round trip.
From performance-first, take tier-1 IR inlining through the llvmbpf overlay between optimizeModule and codegen, as a later slice.

From performance-first, take the eligibility scan over all cuda__ handlers at init_attach_ctx_from_handlers (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:190-285), so pointer writers are known before any ledger exists instead of being discovered link by link.
From performance-first, take the witness-ring (1527) oracle in test builds and the step-0 %globaltimer breakdown of host_call.
From performance-first, take its measurement discipline: re-measure the baseline at 52126f33 (AC3 watcher) and add large-geometry cases (100k and 1M threads) where serialization dominates.
From performance-first, take BPFTIME_GPU_PRINTK_SYNC=1 as an opt-out for tools that need printk interleaved in real time with host output (launchlate).
must_fix: Hook every host access path to a ledgered HASH map. That includes the typed fast paths map_lookup_hash, map_update_hash and map_delete_hash (map_handler.cpp:302,336,355), which CPU programs reach through bpftime_hash_map_*_elem_helper (bpf_helper.cpp:470-622, selected at bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:499-555). Add a test with a CPU probe whose program uses only HASH maps.

Make upsert creation independent of the delta value. Keep a per-slot count published as one consistent snapshot with the sum, or send groups whose Σd ≡ 0 (mod 2^64) through the exact host fallback. Add a test that inserts with d = 0 after a host delete.

Never publish pending state that spans several words as unordered stores or reductions. Sum and count, or a version and its payload, must be read as one snapshot: by fence order plus a stated read order, a seqlock under a device lock, or a single word. Prove that a host delete or update cannot resurrect a key or drop a delta.

If incarnations or two-half seqlocks are kept, show that a host cut cannot lose old-incarnation data when GPU commits land during its read. For example, use a transient CUTTING state that makes GPU commits abort and retry, or a host acknowledgement before the stale half may be overwritten. Add a mutation test for exactly this interleaving.

The core exactness argument may rely only on CPU-GPU memory facts already relied on at 52126f33: GPU atomics among GPU threads on segment memory, and fence-then-flag message passing in both directions. Any extra fact (store buffering, cross-context GPU atomics on sysmem, visibility of unfenced posted reductions, 64-bit single-copy atomicity) must be a capability bit measured at start-up, and deferral must be switched off when it fails.

Give the reference semantics a real-time clause, and give deferred units a commit point that ends before the helper returns (a system-scope fence). Scope ordering claims per map unless fences make cross-map program order hold.

State exactly what a host read guarantees when pending state spans several ledgers or shards (several agents, SM shards): regular and monotone, or linearizable. Provide a strict mode, and record the anomaly in R1 rather than leaving it implicit.

Specify a fold or merge function for every effect kind (ADD, SET, DEL, add-if-present). Say which writes are in place and which are replacements, and how each interacts with lock-free hash lookups (bpftime_hash_map.hpp:112-134) and with pointers held by CPU probes and synchronous GPU lanes (:528-538).
Make the loader's value copy part of the fold or merge section. Today it is a memcpy after the lookup returns, outside any lock (syscall_context.cpp:615-622).

A DEFER-to-SYNC flip, or the arrival of a late pointer-writer or unfusible program, must not allow a CPU in-place fold and a GPU pointer write on the same word. Either drain in-flight deferred helpers with a stated handshake, or decide pointer writers over all handlers before any ledger exists. A late link must still attach within a bounded time, even when unseen graph or CUDA 13 handle launches prevent proving quiescence.

Define the outcome of CPU plain stores through a pointer into a map with pending GPU effects. Either classify them and keep the map synchronous, or state the non-Linux outcome (pending effects applied on top of a later store) as a deviation.

Any GPU-local read that copies into the probe's stack must account for memcapture's prepended `r10 -= len` and line stores (ptxpass_kprobe_memcapture/main.cpp:63-127), or be disabled under memcapture. Validate the stack bound after the pass's own prepending, not before.

Keep presence and capacity (max_entries, E2BIG) host-linearized, through a host-side attach or claim on first touch. Do not use a GPU/CPU counter pair that needs store buffering, and test the full-map case.
Keep every committed effect host-reachable without the agent, including after an agent SIGKILL, also on discrete GPUs. Otherwise declare the loss as a deviation from exactness.

Fallbacks (ledger full, mode change, closed map, generation mismatch) must stay exact and cost one request per group. Unregistered helper ids must be impossible: register them in core.cpp:234-253, test that every emitted id is registered, and gate on a pass capability symbol.
Bound the cost of hot keys: give a sharding or aggregation option for constant keys on uncached segment memory, chosen by the measured c_atom_sys under contention before any speedup is claimed.

For R7, the headline check is the per-record decision against the survey's operation and result_use. Present class (20/39/0) as derived from the input column cpu_reads_map. Report aggregatable as 47 + 4 listed timing records, since the survey's 51 follows no consistent rule. Emit one record per incoming edge for clang-merged calls (cuda-counter retprobe pc 76), and build rocm-counter for the check.

Prerequisite or documented limitation: the one CommSharedMem is shared by every agent on the segment, and each agent zeroes it at start (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:615). Fallback host ops and any attach opcode inherit that hazard.

strengths: The analyzer sits where the inputs and the segment are both reachable: bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:636-648 calls create_map_basic_info(1024) and then create_attach_with_ebpf_callback, and it copies prog->get_insns() into nv_attach_private_data.instructions. Rewriting there changes only the attach copy and leaves the nv_attach_impl interface as it is. nv_attach_impl itself has no segment access (no shm_holder or handler_manager in attach/nv_attach_impl/*.cpp, checked).

The carrier works with the code as it is. Unregistered ids really do exit: compiler_utils.cpp:331-370 returns 'Ext func not found', which reaches exitOnErr (llvm_jit_context.cpp:907, 936-939) because kernel_compatible_mode is false (compiler.cpp:1471-1475). The design registers ids 600-604 next to core.cpp:234-253. The names _bpf_helper_ext_0600 match the extern filter regex at core.cpp:280-283 (ext_func_sym pads to 4 digits, compiler_utils.hpp:39-44). A dlsym capability gate is feasible because passes are already resolved with dlsym(handle, print_config/process_input) at nv_attach_impl.cpp:601-614.

The pointer to the ledger fits the existing map_info layout. The trampoline routes on extra_buffer only for ARRAY (default_trampoline.cu:271), so a ledger address in a HASH entry's extra_buffer changes no current path. The module global is written on all three load paths, all checked: nv_attach_impl.cpp:2366-2385, 1323-1352 and nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:263-292.

The weakest hardware assumptions of the three. The fold reads GPU-written words only with loads, every word has a single writer, and it never waits for the GPU. It needs GPU-to-CPU message passing and GPU-GPU atomicity, not CPU-GPU store buffering.

The most complete soundness rule for pointer writers. Any GPU pointer write keeps the map out of DEFER. On the CPU only atomic adds are allowed, and only next to add-only ledgers. A late writer flips the map to SYNC instead of waiting for quiescence.

Slice 1 gives the largest and most convincing measurable result. It defers A and B in CUDA Counter, removing 3 of the 8 host calls per thread: 264 to 160 requests per launch, about 2,877 to 1,760 us, and call_count 97 to 128. The numbers agree with hostcall-l1-20261111/README.md: 1,312 to 1,056 requests over 4 launches, 2,877.5 us.

The R7 check was simulated (r7_output.txt). It gives 0 mismatches between decision and (operation, result_use) and reproduces 20/39/0. The design states openly that the class check is nearly vacuous, and it explains the 51 as 47 yes + 8 timing + 4 no, the 8 timing sites listed.

The oracles are independent of the mechanism: closed-form N*L, a per-thread delta sum in a 1512 map, a lookup_and_delete stress (T3) and a torn-read test (T8). Each mutation names the test it must fail.
flaws: The fold hook misses the typed HASH fast paths. A CPU program whose maps are all HASH gets bpftime_hash_map_lookup_elem_helper (wired at bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:443-449). That helper calls map_lookup_hash directly (bpf_helper.cpp:492, 595, 621 into map_handler.cpp:302, 336, 355), not map_lookup_elem. CPU probes would read unfolded values, the epoch would not be bumped, and the claim 'every path converges at the handler entry points' is false. T4 uses a pre-populated key with an in-place add, so it would not catch this.

The warp grouping scratch is indexed by (%smid, %warpid). PTX documents %warpid as unique within a CTA, not within an SM (external, inferred; not checked locally), so co-resident CTAs can share an entry. The order 'tag, __syncwarp, then read keys and values' is racy between two live warps, so the claim that it 'only loses aggregation' does not hold as written. This path is in slice 1 (threadscheduling keys on %smid).

Fold-on-access adds a stripe lock to lookups that take no lock today (bpftime_hash_map.hpp:112-134: 'Lookups take no lock'; map_handler.cpp:303). The design adds no fast path for a key with nothing pending, and it does not plan to measure the regression on CPU-probe and loader lookups.

Slice 1 is too large for about 5 weeks. It has a ~3k-line port with a value-number lattice, a general jump-fixup patcher, re-analysis by value-number comparison, an analyzer for CPU programs, every handler hook, gen and DEAD, and the capability gate. In-place NOP padding fits every slice-1 region (cuda-counter entry pc 22-37, 16 slots; retprobe pc 28-35, 8 slots; micro hash_lookup pc 68-74, 7 slots; checked in the disassembly), so the fixup patcher is unnecessary for now.

The reason for disabling res_lookup under memcapture is wrong. memcapture moves r10 down with SUB64_IMM by the line length rounded to 8 and stores the line above the new r10 (ptxpass_kprobe_memcapture/main.cpp:63-90). The real constraint is shift + program depth + reserved slot <= 512, and only the pass knows the shift.
The cost of contended atom.add on one uncached host word (constant pid key, xlarge) is unknown. No step-0 calibration runs before building, so the xlarge projection has no anchor.

The slot size is stated inconsistently: 'padded to 64 B' in the layout, ~128-192 B in the examples. The slot-claim protocol does not say that a group finding a CLAIMING slot must wait, which is what prevents two slots for one key.
The mode-flip residual window (a CPU plain store during DEFER to SYNC) is left open, and R10 has no test for the flip.

strengths: The most measurable plan. Its anchors check out against the results: baseline-sub-20261111/summary.md:22 gives CUDA Counter 2,928.9 us and README.md:31 gives calls=97; GPU Array lookup/update (large) are 65.9 and 242.4 us. Step 0 instruments host_call with %globaltimer to break down the ~10 us, and measures red throughput at 1, 32, 3,136 and 31,264 warps before anything is built. The geometry series (minimal, 1,024 and 100,352 threads, key = lane%4) is what shows threads x calls going away. It also says the baseline must be re-measured at 52126f33.
The smallest slice: idiom A only, tier 0, Orin. The A-only projection is self-consistent: 1 of 8 calls, about -12%, calls=128.

The per-map eligibility scan is feasible where it is placed. init_attach_ctx_from_handlers instantiates every non-CUDA handler in its first loop and the CUDA links in its second (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:190-285), so every cuda__ program is known before any module runs.
The witness ring through 1527 gives an oracle that does not depend on the overlay code. The mutation list targets the grouping mask, the offsets and 32-bit tearing.

It describes the memcapture r10 shift correctly (SUB64_IMM, main.cpp:63-90). It gives a sound O3 fallback: a phi'd site id selects the generic helper. Inline-asm PTX avoids LLVM 15 selecting sm_70+ instructions from an sm_61 target (Makefile: PTX_TARGET_ARCH sm_61, PTX 8.1).
The single-writer rule with CPU-side offsets avoids CPU-GPU atomic RMW, and the 1527 ring is its precedent.
flaws: SEALING waits for quiescence. With the unseen-launch latch set (graphs, CUDA 13 handle launches) a late link can be deferred indefinitely, which is a liveness and usability problem in this codebase.

The capacity admission needs store buffering, which the design does not acknowledge. The GPU reads cpu_new_keys and increments gpu_claims, while the CPU inserts against gpu_claims. Each side can miss the other's increment, so max_entries can be exceeded. This contradicts the claim that only message passing is needed.
lww.lock lives in segment memory, so contended LWW stores spin on host memory, the 300 us case that default_trampoline.cu:118-121 warns about.

Slice 1 depends on PTX that has never been tested: match.any and redux as inline asm in a trampoline built for sm_61 and retargeted to sm_87. It needs a second trampoline variant for devices below sm_70. Tier 1 needs a new llvm_jit_context overlay hunk, a new compile_ebpf_to_ptx_from_words overload and a new llvmbpf_vm setter.

Posted red.add with no fence relies on visibility of GPU writes to a CPU reader during the kernel, which BRIEF lists as open. Its read test only checks 'monotonic, never above final', a one-sided bound.

The merge layer is described only as 'libbpftime's map layer'. It does not list the typed HASH fast paths (map_handler.cpp:302-367). Materializing a key in place through with_existing_value can race with a CPU probe's plain RMW and lose folded GPU deltas.

On a discrete GPU the overlay is in agent device memory with a 100 ms mirror. A SIGKILL then loses committed effects, so the guarantee depends on the hardware, against the requirement that hardware enter only as cost parameters.
There is no runnable R7 pre-check (check_plan.py is only proposed). Its aggregatable count of 53 under 'upstream's rule' uses a different rule from the other two designs' 55.

strengths: The most rigorous reference semantics: per-key linearizability plus a host-owned presence and capacity object, composed by locality. Every hardware assumption (A1-A5) is stated, and step-0 litmus tests run against a reader in another process.

Its host entry-point list is the only correct one. It names the typed fast paths map_lookup_hash, map_update_hash and map_delete_hash (map_handler.cpp:302-367) used by bpf_helper.cpp:470-622, and notes that the hook must not go into bpftime_hash_map, which per-CPU hash also uses.

In-place NOP-padding rewrite with no jump fixups. Checked in the disassembly: the retprobe B unit fits pc 28-35, and r0 and r1-r5 are dead at pc 77. It also adds self-validation of the rewritten words and recommends replacing the static ExitOnError (llvm_jit_context.cpp:907).

T8 is differential translation validation against the CPU llvmbpf JIT, with near-miss fixtures. T2 is a two-sided real-time bound using CLOCK_MONOTONIC brackets. Both are the strongest exactness tests in the three designs.
ATTACH makes first touch and E2BIG exact against Linux's ordering. Two-level locking (device-memory lock, then host version word) mirrors host_call's own fix (default_trampoline.cu:118-122).
flaws: Every deferred host write rests on A3, CPU<->GPU store buffering, which the design itself says has no evidence. Its gate also requires the fence-free negative control to show violations; if uncached GPU accesses are strongly ordered it never will, so the gate cannot pass by its own rule.

A pointer-writer hole: nothing excludes a PES map that also has unrecognised GPU pointer-RMW sites (kept SYNC) or CPU plain RMW. Fold-before-return and the periodic watcher fold add into the base element in place while a plain read-modify-write is running, which loses contributions committed before the RMW began. The kind check in R7.3 does not cover this.

No capability gate on the pass. pes_abi in RuntimeInput is ignored by an old pass, which then compiles ids 520-525 and exits the application (compiler_utils.cpp:370 into llvm_jit_context.cpp:936-939).

# UnitFold: exact per-call-site execution of GPU eBPF helper calls

Final design for direction 2 (GPU-to-CPU host calls). It merges three drafts (analysis-first, semantics-first, performance-first) after two reviews; both reviews chose analysis-first as the base. A longer version with the same decisions and more detail (full test and mutation tables, must-fix coverage tables) is at `/tmp/claude-2002/-home-jetson-src/6ac0883f-4479-466c-bec5-5fa31cffe4de/scratchpad/dir2-design/final/design.md`. The R7 simulation is `.../dir2-design/final/r7_check.py`, `r7_output.txt` and `r7_records.json`.

**Conventions.**
- Every `path:line` is in `/home/jetson/src/bpftime-daily-state/worktrees/4708f4092d1e/candidate` at 52126f33, re-read for this document. llvmbpf lines refer to submodule `vm/llvm-jit` at 87bac39a, before the overlay.
- **[new]** marks a mechanism invented here. **[inferred]** marks reasoning over code that was never run. **[external]** marks CUDA/PTX documentation not re-read.
- Nothing was built and nothing ran on the GPU. Only Python ran, over `records.json`.

## Overview

### The problem

**When a helper call becomes a host call.** A GPU probe's helper call turns into a synchronous host call for:
- HASH maps and other CPU maps;
- 1501, which is created as HASH on the Orin (`runtime/include/bpftime_shm.hpp:137-154`, applied at `runtime/syscall-server/syscall_context.cpp:566-577`);
- every delete except on ordinary ARRAY;
- printk and puts.

The routing is in `attach/nv_attach_impl/trampoline/default_trampoline.cu:233-422`.

**How a host call works.**
1. Take the module device lock.
2. Take `occupy_flag` in the segment's single `CommSharedMem`.
3. Write the request, execute `membar.sys`, set `flag1`, spin on `flag2`. Lanes take turns over a 32-step loop (`default_trampoline.cu:134-175`).
4. The watcher takes `flag1` with an acquire CAS and answers with a release store of `flag2` (`runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:309, 317`).

**Measured** (aa6eb973, `hostcall-l1-20261111/README.md:26-41`):

| case | per launch | note |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 39.9 us | |
| CPU Array lookup (served on the GPU since 1b3d9c99) | 48.2 us | |
| CPU Hash lookup | 341.1 us | |
| CUDA Counter | 2,877.5 us | 264 requests per launch (8 per thread + first-touch inserts) |

- This gives about 10.7 us per host call.
- At 52126f33 (AC3 watcher) a call in a 32-call burst costs 11.8 us without load and 15.7 us under load (`watcher-policy-20261112/v3/README.md:57-58`).
- **Data loss today.** The CUDA Counter loader prints `calls=97` in every run (`hostcall-l1-20261111/README.md:32-33`) where 128 probes ran.
  - All 32 lookups of a warp are answered before any lane branches.
  - The 32 first-touch `BPF_NOEXIST` inserts race and one lands.
  - A plain `*v += d` through the shared pointer collapses to about one update per warp.
- **Survey baseline.** The survey classifies 168 GPU sites as 109 already GPU-local, 20 eliminate, 39 defer, 0 sync; 51 of the 59 host-call sites are marked aggregatable.

### What UnitFold does

**Units.** A load-time analyzer in the agent recognises multi-instruction idioms (lookup + add or insert) as one *unit*. It rewrites each unit in the bytecode into one call of a new registered helper (ids 600-604), with the site descriptor in immediates (no pc).

**Commit.** The GPU commits a deferred unit with plain stores into a seqlocked *record* in the shared segment and executes `membar.sys` before returning. There is no round trip. Lanes with an equal key are reduced first.

**Fold.** Every host access path folds the key's committed records into the map under the key's stripe lock, right before its own operation. That covers loader `bpf()` commands, CPU probes in the agent and watcher-served calls. So host state is current at every host access, with:
- no flush;
- no kernel-completion hook;
- no loader-to-agent channel;
- no CPU-GPU atomics;
- no store-buffering assumption.

**Fallback.** The first touch of a key is a synchronous host operation, so presence and capacity stay host-decided. Whatever cannot be proven keeps today's path. Hardware enters only as measured costs and litmus-tested capability bits.

| task mode | UnitFold mechanism |
|---|---|
| eliminate | records that no host ever folds; an ABSENT negative cache makes add-if-present and delete of absent keys free. GPU-local reads (READ_LOCAL) only with store buffering (R3.7), else one LOOKUP_COPY per group |
| aggregate | lanes with an equal key commit once with the lane count and the sum of deltas |
| defer | record commit (ADD, SET, DEL) or printk ring record |
| sync round trip | today's `call 1/2/3/6`, unchanged; new host operations UNIT_ADD, UNIT_SET, UNIT_DEL and LOOKUP_COPY serve as exact per-group fallbacks |

### Coined names

| name | meaning |
|---|---|
| unit | an idiom, any other helper call, or one BPF_ATOMIC instruction, executed as one atomic step |
| ledger [new] | per-map structure in the segment holding unfolded GPU effects |
| slot | one key's entry in a ledger; only the host creates slots, so a key has at most one |
| record [new] | per (slot, shard): a version word `ver` plus two halves of cumulative totals. GPU-written, zeroed once by the CPU at slot creation |
| shadow [new] | the GPU's device-memory copy of a record |
| watermark | the CPU-only copy of what has been folded |
| fold | applying record deltas to the element under the stripe lock |
| straggler | a GPU commit landing after a host operation's read; ordered after that operation |
| hint | CPU-written slot state (LIVE, ABSENT, DEAD) that the GPU reads |
| device block [new] | per (ledger, agent) device memory: lock table, shadows, key-to-slot cache, `devmode` |
| flip [new] | agent-local drain when a late pointer writer appears |
| sweep [new] | folding pending re-creations before capacity-changing operations |
| strict mode | the default: one record per slot (S = 1) and one deferring agent per map |

### What changes

| between the two loops of `init_attach_ctx_from_handlers` (`runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:229-245` / `:248-259`) | analyzer over all handlers; ledgers |

**Unchanged:** the request protocol, lane serialisation, the watcher's sleep policies, GPU map types, the ARRAY path, loaders and tools.

## R1. Reference semantics

### Actions

**Actions.**
- **GPU units** (per thread, in program order across its probe executions).
- **Host operations:**
  - loader `bpf()` map commands, run in the loader process on the segment (`syscall_context.cpp:600-679`);
  - CPU-probe helpers (`bpf_helper.cpp:401-422, 470-622`);
  - watcher-served requests (`bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:124-187`);
  - close.
- **printk lines.**

**Plain pointer accesses** outside units are data races, as in Linux.

**Precondition PW** [new, enforced in R3.6]. On a ledgered map, no attached program does any of the following through a lookup pointer:
- a plain store;
- a non-ADD atomic;
- on the GPU, any atomic.

The only exception is D5.

**Commit point.** A deferred unit commits at the even `ver` store of its record. A `membar.sys` follows before the helper returns.

**hb (happens-before)** is the closure of:
- program order;
- fence-then-flag message passing in either direction;
- kernel completion observed by stream, device or event synchronisation;
- CPU synchronisation.

Real time between CPU and GPU is only observable through these.

### SR: the reference

An execution is **exact** if, for every map M, there is a total order ≺ over the units and host operations on M such that:
1. **(po)** each thread's program order holds;
2. **(rt)** if end(a) hb start(b), then a ≺ b;
3. **(seq)** replaying ≺ on Linux's sequential specification gives every value returned to a probe, every host return value, every host read and the final contents.

The specification includes flags, EEXIST, ENOENT and E2BIG (`kernel/bpf/hashtab.c:1084-1113`, L4T 6.8.12). A unit replays as its own instructions, executed atomically.

- **printk:** per agent, (po) and (rt), and every line appears exactly once.
- **Measured against:** this order, not today's bpftime, which no order explains (97 of 128).
- **Scope:** per map, like Linux. Commits are fenced, so a host reader that sees a thread's later commit on any map also sees its earlier ones (message passing). This is not cross-map atomicity.

### Observation points

**Every host access** through the `bpf_map_handler` entry points of R3.5, in any process, reflects every unit whose end hb its start. This needs no kernel completion, flush, launch tracking or live agent.

- `get_next_key(NULL)` sweeps first.
- An iteration in progress may miss later re-creations, like Linux.
- Excluded: ARRAY mmap (`syscall_context.cpp:1036-1048`); batch commands, which fall through to the real `bpf()` (`syscall_context.cpp:852-854`); `run_with_kernel`.

### Per idiom

Linux guarantees atomicity per helper call and per BPF_ATOMIC. Beyond that:
- plain RMW is racy;
- miss followed by NOEXIST loses increments;
- update replaces the element;
- user reads copy one element;
- printk merges by timestamp and can lose lines.

Every SR execution is a Linux-legal serial schedule, so UnitFold refines Linux except D1-D6.

| idiom (sites) | Linux | today | UnitFold | vs Linux |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A counter: lookup; miss → NOEXIST insert; hit → atomic add (10) | first-touch loss | 97/128 | ADD-or-create; first touch is a host operation | more |
| B non-atomic RMW, EXIST self-write, else NOEXIST (9) | lost updates | ~1 per warp | ADD-or-create, exact Σ | more |
| C leader lookup + update(ANY, `p?*p+d:d`) (4) | racy across launches | exact unless overlapping | ADD-or-create | more |
| E entry SET / exit READ / DEL (9) | per call | per call | SET and DEL deferred; READ via LOOKUP_COPY (READ_LOCAL with C-SB) | same |
| F per-thread record (2) | per call | same | SET; E2BIG decided at a host first touch | same |
| G leader publish (1) | per call | same | SET | same |
| H printk (21) | per-CPU order, may lose | synchronous | per-thread order, no loss, ≤ 1 watcher turn late | same / more / less (D3) |
| J benchmark: update / lookup + `(*v)++` / delete (3) | `++` racy | collapses | SET / ADD-if-present / DEL | same / more / same |
| unrecognised pointer RMW | racy | racy | map not ledgered | same |

In strict mode, host reads are linearizable: one record per key, one seqlock snapshot.

### Deviations, each counted

- **D1 (opt-in only: shards S > 1 or several deferring agents).**
  - Host reads during commits are regular and monotone; they are linearizable only if a double collect of `ver` is stable.
  - A destructive operation splits records at their own reads.
  - Conservation stays exact.
  - Counter: `unstable_reads`.
- **D2.** Commits on a closed map are dropped. bpftime frees maps on close (`runtime/src/handler/handler_manager.cpp:116-123`); in Linux the effect would be unobservable. Counter: `dead_drops`.
- **D3.** printk appears up to one watcher turn late. The backstop is 1,000 us (`runtime/src/attach/cuda_watcher_policy.hpp:27`). Opt-out: `BPFTIME_GPU_PRINTK_SYSNC` is not a typo-free name, so use `BPFTIME_GPU_PRINTK_SYNC=1`.
- **D4.** A straggler re-creating a host-deleted key gets its E2BIG decision at the first sweep or fold that sees it.
  - Sweeps run before every insert and delete near capacity.
  - What remains: when several stragglers are pending on a nearly full map, which ones get in follows sweep order.
  - Counter: `e2big_sweep`.
- **D5.** If a flip times out (`T_flip` = 1 s):
  - late commits are applied by element replacement, never in place;
  - a concurrent write through an old pointer can be lost (Linux's update semantics, triggered by the fold).
  - Counter: `late_stragglers`.
- **D6.** Deferred GPU writes after `BPF_MAP_FREEZE` are applied, as Linux allows for programs. Today GPU host calls get EPERM (`runtime/src/handler/map_handler.cpp:445-448, 776-779`). UNIT_* operations use program semantics; unrewritten sites keep EPERM.

### Proof sketch (strict mode, ADD; SET and DEL analogous)

- **Invariant I.** A ledgered key's element changes only:
  - in a fold;
  - in a host operation run right after a fold under the same stripe lock;
  - by commuting CPU atomic adds through pointers.

  It rests on PW and on full hook coverage.
- **Lemma 1 (snapshot).** The two-half read returns totals held at one instant. It needs H2 and H4, and never waits on an odd `ver`.
- **Lemma 2 (fold).**
  - The deltas s − w met an unchanged element (Invariant I). Adds commute, and the count decides re-creation, so applying them at the fold equals applying them at their commits.
  - Commits whose end hb the fold's start are in s (H2 plus the trailing fence).
  - Later ones are ordered after the operation.
- **Lemma 3.** Each lane is in exactly one equal-key group; the count is the lane count.
- **Lemma 4 (presence and capacity).**
  - Every key insertion is a host operation: a UNIT_* first touch, a host insert, or a fold re-creation.
  - Count-changing operations sweep first near capacity.
  - Pending GPU DELs are folded before an E2BIG.
  - Therefore the base map's accounting linearizes presence and capacity, except D4's order.
- **Theorem.** Per-key objects and the capacity object are linearizable. By locality (Herlihy-Wing), SR holds.

## R2. Difference from gpu_ext and upstream automatic warp execution

From `overlap-survey-20261113/README.md:44-60`:
- **gpu_ext** (ASPLOS '27) claims warp-leader shards merged at kernel completion with "relaxed, eventual consistency". Its own audit found no implementation. Its results come from hand-rewritten tools.
- **Upstream `official/revision/automatic-warp-execution`** is unmerged and opt-in.
  - It decides yes or no per program.
  - It rejects atomics, printk, puts, perf output, exit and per-thread writes.
  - It runs admitted programs in the leader lane, and a non-atomic `*v = *v + 1` counts once per converged group.

| | gpu_ext | auto-warp | UnitFold |
|---|---|---|---|
| reference | eventual | equivalence to today's collapse | SR with an hb clause, oracle-tested |
| unit of decision | tool, by hand | program | call site or idiom, per-site fallback |
| host sees effects | after a completion merge | immediately (nothing deferred) | at every access: the reader folds |
| aggregation | leader election | leader election | reduction: Σ deltas plus lane count |
| host writes against deferred effects | no rule | n/a | fold-then-operate puts every commit on one side |
| atomics, printk, CPU maps | avoided | rejected | supported per site |
| storage | workload-fitted | none | sized by keys; full → exact sync fallback |
| hardware | unstated | `vote.ballot` | message passing plus 8-byte atomicity, litmus-gated |

**Why exact.**
- Effects are cumulative totals composed at fold time with the value they would have met.
- No merge point exists. The hooks do not see completion of graph launches or CUDA 13 handle launches (`nv_attach_impl.cpp:1561-1592`; `probed_launch_activity.cpp:16-24`).
- Aggregation is a reduction over equal key bytes.
- Storage pressure falls back to the exact host path.

**Why per site.** Each unit has its own descriptor, fallback and grouping. A `%s` printk stays synchronous while its program's counters are deferred.

## R3. Dynamic answer to "only GPU probes touch this map"

UnitFold never needs that fact: every host path composes GPU effects at access time.

### R3.1 Hardware facts

Each core fact is litmus-checked at start-up. Deferral is enabled only if H2-H4 pass.

| id | fact | precedent at 52126f33 |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | GPU atomics within one context on device memory | module lock (`default_trampoline.cu:118-122, 146-148`) |
| H2 | GPU→CPU message passing to a reader **in another process**: stores, `membar.sys`, flag; reader acquire | 1527 tail (`default_trampoline.cu:478-480`) drained by the loader (`nv_gpu_ringbuf_map.cpp:65-68`) |
| H3 | CPU→GPU message passing | `flag2` release (`bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:317`) → GPU spin + `membar.sys` (`default_trampoline.cu:159-163`); 1527 head (`:461-470`) |
| H4 | 8-byte single-copy atomicity on the segment | 1527 u64 head/tail (`gpu_helper_protocol.h:86-103`) |
| H5 | GPU-scope ordering: `bar.warp.sync`, device-lock acquire/release | standard PTX [external]; `__syncwarp` and CAS locks in use |

**Never needed:** GPU atomics on the segment, CPU-GPU atomic RMW, store buffering, CPU posting into `CommSharedMem` (`occupy_flag` is GPU-only, `default_trampoline.cu:149`).

**Capability bits** (measured, optional):
- **C-SB** (CPU-GPU store buffering) → READ_LOCAL.
- **C-XA** (cross-context sysmem atomics) → optional shared single-word records.
- **C-PTX** (`shfl`, `match.any`, `redux`, `vote`, `nanosleep` text accepted after the sm_87 retarget, `nv_attach_utils.cpp:52-65`) → faster grouping.
- **C-SCHED** (an agent kernel gets scheduled while application kernels occupy the GPU) → exact flip.

### R3.2 Layout

**Ledger** [new], in the Boost segment.
- Allocated by the agent, as for its alive-pid set (`runtime/agent/agent.cpp:1195-1199`).
- The segment is `cuMemHostRegister`ed by every agent (`bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1407-1475`), so the loader reads it without the agent.
- Contents:
  - header (CPU-written): fd, `gen`, sizes, kind (UPSERT_ADD with template c, ADD_IF_PRESENT, LWW), add field (aligned, 4 or 8 bytes), C, S, owner pid, mode hint, flip request and ack, statistics;
  - CPU index: 2C entries; slots created under a ledger mutex;
  - per-slot hint;
  - CPU watermarks;
  - absent list;
  - records per (slot, shard): `ver` plus two halves. ADD halves hold {sum, count}; LWW halves add {wseq, wkind, sum_at, count_at, value}.

**Device block** [new], agent `cuMemAlloc` in the primary context (`bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:262-276`):
- `devmode`, written only by the agent's flip kernel;
